findings.where: results/flow_state.json outcome_caveat, clause 'the hourly flow is the gauge's own record, an input a real-time service has' (code/22_flow_state.py, the outcome_caveat f-string); the same words in the figure footer (draw())
findings.text: The clause overstates what was tested. Every hourly value used here is from the APPROVED record (approved share 1.0 in all 12 gauges, data_coverage), and the 24:00 variant reads the hour that ends at the issue time itself, i.e. it assumes zero delivery delay; a real-time service gets PROVISIONAL values (revised later, most at high flow, when shifts and rating changes are applied) with the telemetry delay of the gauge (USGS transmits most stations hourly, some every four hours). The 22:00 variant covers a delay of at most two hours and is the conservative one of the two only against such a delay. Since the documents print outcome_full word for word once this review exists (code/build_slides_final.py: e4e_reviewed -> N('e4e_outcome_full')), the sentence must carry the two qualifications. Fix (replace the clause): 'the hourly flow is the gauge's own record, an input a real-time service has as provisional values and after a delivery delay (the 24:00 variant assumes none and the 22:00 variant two hours; this study used the approved record), while the AORC rain to midnight is an analysis made after the fact (hindsight at most about 3 points) for the daily total; the within-day columns of wqaWH_s and wqaWHF_s have no such measurement'. State the same in design.what or a note: 'the 24:00 variant assumes zero delivery delay and approved values'.

findings.where: figures/flow_state.png, top panel (code/22_flow_state.py draw(): the line at 70 with the text 'GO asks 70% warned (at most 30% false)' and the bar labels)
findings.text: The wqaWHF22_s bar is labelled 70% and sits on the line labelled 'GO asks 70% warned (at most 30% false)', and no false share appears anywhere on the figure; its false share is 42.1% (verdict CAUTION, operating_points.sets.wqaWHF22_s.l1.rules.plain), and no set of this experiment meets the GO false share at trigger 1.0 (false shares 37.6% to 55.4%; at the 30%-false operating point the best realistic set warns of 50.7%). A reader of the figure alone takes the bar as GO. Fix: print the false share with every bar label from summary_test (e.g. '70%\n42% false') and change the line's text to 'GO asks 70% warned AND at most 30% false: no bar here keeps the false share under 30% at trigger 1.0', or draw the 30%-false operating points as a second mark on each bar (operating_points far_cap test pod).

'Sets, inputs, seeds, stopping rule and the success rule ... were fixed in NEXT_EXPERIMENTS_2026-10-28.md and in this script before training': the work order's E4e section names no seed count (its table row says 'a night + 10-20 trainings'; E4b's section says 'three seeds, then five'), the script's default is three, and the run was launched with --seeds 5 in one pass (honest: before any test score was seen; h1: one training pass, seeds [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]). The seed count decides the verdict here: with the first three seeds the rule would be MET (wqaH_s seeds 0-2: 47.2, 48.4, 47.5% against wqa_s 33.1, 42.1, 46.9%), and it fails only because seeds [3, 4] (46.6%, 45.7%) fall below the best wqa_s seed (46.9%). Fix: 'Five seeds were chosen at launch (--seeds 5; the script's default is three; the work order names no count), before any test score was seen; with the first three seeds the rule would be met' in choices, and e4e_success.met_with_first_three_seeds = true beside met = false. The spread of wqa_s's three seeds (13.7 points) against 2.7 for wqaH_s is why an 'every seed above every seed' rule is fragile against a three-seed base; the seed-mean of wqaH_s is above every wqa_s seed.

The pre-registered rule (wqaH_s above wqa_s in every seed at lead 1, pooled onsets at trigger 1.0) is NOT met with the five seeds, as the file says; the seed-mean gain of +6.6 points is 'no clear difference' by the onset seed rule and 'clear gain' in NSE (every seed above, 11 of 12 basins, p = 0.001), with 41 onsets warned only with the river's state against 19 only without (sign p = 0.006). Unlike E4b, the validation years foreshadow it: onsets warned 49.0% against 43.4% at trigger 1.0, every wqaH_s seed (46.5% to 51.5%) above every wqa_s seed (41.4% to 44.9%).

Turkey Creek's 328 fallback test days lie in two outages (2011-09-05 to 2012-01-22 (140 days), 2012-05-03 to 2012-11-04 (186 days)) that hold none of its 21 lead-1 test onsets, so its onset table is the same with and without them (12 hits, 7 false alarms for wqaH_s against 12 and 14 for wqa_s); its lead-1 NSE is 0.835 on all test days and 0.828 on the targets whose issue day is known (wqa_s 0.776 and 0.770). Pooled, 14 of the 335 lead-1 onsets have a fallback issue day: wqaH_s warns 3 of them against 6 for wqa_s, and on the other 321 48.6% against 40.8%: the fallback days cost the new columns about three hits, nothing more.

findings.where: code/22_flow_state.py docstring and MISMATCH_REL comment ('South Toe on 17 Sep 2004, 53 against 175 mm/day'); data_coverage.mismatch_days_24
findings.text: In the 24:00 variant none of the 20 mismatch days is decided by the mismatch rule alone: every one already has hours missing after the carry (the gap rule sends it to the fallback first); in the 22:00 variant the rule alone decides 5 days (a rise in the last two hours). The docstring's example is such a gap day: 17 Sep 2004 has one hour with values (the hour ending 24:00, 52.6 mm/day), 17 hours still missing after the carry, a mean over the available hours of 36.6 against the daily mean 175.5; '53' is the one known hour, not the quantity the rule compares. Harmless; the rule is a second guard.

findings.where: results/flow_state.json data_coverage.per_basin.*.local_day_mean_vs_camels; code/22_flow_state.py flow_state_table (the wall clock with summer time)
findings.text: The USGS daily mean's day follows the wall clock with summer time in 10 of 12 gauges (the script's convention: in June-August the local-day mean of the hourly flow reproduces the CAMELS daily mean better with it), but standard time all year fits better at Murder Creek (02221525) and Turkey Creek (02349900): there the script's 24:00 in summer is 23:00 standard time, one hour before the end of the USGS day, so the columns read one hour LESS than the daily mean, never more (no leakage); the daily mean q_mm of day t, an input of every model of the project, then covers one hour after the issue time at those two gauges in summer: a project-wide convention, not E4e's (h3 usgs_daily_value_clock).

On this PC all 30 networks reproduce their stored forecasts bit for bit with one torch thread (the run used 4), on tables built as the script builds them and on tables whose hourly-flow columns are the reviewer's own (which equal the script's bit for bit on every day); the scalers inside every file equal the training-row statistics; the reviewer's made-up-hours test (22 cases, two zones, clock-change days included, the script's builder and the reviewer's) and made-up-values test (10 cases on lstm_wqaH_s_s2 and lstm_wqaWHF_s_s1) pass; the three stored sets rescored here equal results/forecast_input.json to 1e-9.

findings.where: results/flow_state.json choices_made_after_looking_at_test_scores and outcome_caveat (code/22_flow_state.py CHOICES, the success clause); every document that quotes E4e
findings.text: The file does not disclose that its three comparison sets (lstm_wqa_s, lstm_wqaF_s, lstm_wqaP_s) gained seeds 3 and 4 on 30 October 2026, after this file's test scores were known (+6.6 points on 29 October). Its only choices entry and the success clause ('five seeds were chosen at launch ... in one training pass before any test score was seen') are about the new sets. For E4e the change matters. The headline gain rose from +6.6 to +8.4 points only because the base fell: wqa_s 40.9% to 39.1% (137 to 131 hits), since its added seeds warn of 31.9% and 40.6%. wqaH_s did not change. The closure of the onset gap rose from 21% to 26% (NSE from 95% to 86%), and wqa_s's 30%-false point moved from 1.50 (14.9%, 24% false) to 1.45 (14.9%, 30% false). Fix: add a CHOICES entry, for example: 'The stored comparison sets lstm_wqa_s, lstm_wqaF_s and lstm_wqaP_s gained seeds 3 and 4 on 30 October 2026 on a second machine (script 18, see its SEED_NOTE), after this file's three-seed comparison was known (+6.6 points); the five-seed base is lower (39.1% against 40.9%), so the gain is now +8.4 points with wqaH_s unchanged; the success rule's verdict is the same (the best wqa_s seed is seed 2, 46.9%, an original seed).' Then rescore.

Every how_to_read says 'a five-seed set against a three-seed stored set gives three entries, seeds 3 and 4 of the new set are not in the list'. No such pair exists now: the stored sets have five seeds and every difference_by_seed_points list has five entries (h2: 0 of 42 lists shorter than the longer seed list). Fix: build the sentence from the seed lists, or drop it when every pair has equal seed lists.

findings.where: code/22_flow_state.py, the review guard (same_record, stored_changed, review_covers, review_line)
findings.text: After round_2 is appended, the next --rescore will claim coverage on the wrong grounds. The record's sha256 changes, so same_record turns False and stored_sets_changed_since_the_review is no longer carried. stored_changed then compares only with the previous results file, which already holds the five-seed hashes, so it is empty. The script hash test passes (record_script_sha256 = the training pass), so review_covers becomes True and review_line quotes the ROUND-1 verdict and counts. Any later edit of the record would do the same, even one that finds the numbers wrong. Fix: compare STORED_NOW with the hashes the review recorded (round_2['stored_sets_reviewed'] when present) and take who, date, verdict and counts from the latest round.

The verdict is not decided by the added seeds. The rule fails because wqaH_s seeds 3 and 4 (46.6%, 45.7%) are not above wqa_s seed 2 (46.9%, an original seed). wqa_s seeds 3 and 4 (31.9%, 40.6%) are far below. met_with_first_three_seeds compares seeds 0-2 of wqaH_s (47.2-48.4%) with all five wqa_s seeds, as seed_count_note says. It would also be met three against three (wqa_s seeds 0-2: 33.1-46.9%). The sentence 'not met with the five seeds and would be with the first three' is right.

Seed 3 of the stored perfect-rain set meets GO for onsets at lead 3 at trigger 1.0 (74.4% warned, 29.99% false; also at the CSI and 30%-false triggers, both 1.0). It is an upper-bound set and lead 3, and the file makes no claim about it. The figure's 'no bar here keeps the false share under 30% at trigger 1.0' concerns the seed means at lead 1 and holds (lowest 37.6%).

Read by eye: header 'five seeds per new set, five per stored set', five dots per bar, every label with its false share, status line NOT YET REVIEWED, footer with the provisional-record clause. The hatched stored bars show the five-seed values (39%, 60%, 71%).

round_2.verdict_text: Every number of results/flow_state.json that depends on the stored sets reproduces exactly from results/preds with my own scoring (9110 values, 0 mismatches). wqaH_s warns of 159 of 335 onsets (47.5%) against 131 (39.1%) for the five-seed wqa_s, +8.4 points, with 45 onsets warned only with the river's state and 17 only without. wqaWHF_s gives 68.4% against 59.7% for wqaF_s. At the 30%-false point wqaH_s gives 37.6% (trigger 1.20) against 14.9% for wqa_s (1.45). The success rule is not met with five seeds and would be with the first three. The six new sets' files are byte-identical to 29 October and their numbers, the delivery table and the data coverage are unchanged (13674 leaves). Every clause of outcome_full, rebuilt from my numbers, is in the text. The fixes are about the record: it does not disclose that the comparison sets gained seeds 3-4 after its test scores were known, which alone raised the headline gain from +6.6 to +8.4 points (must-fix); the how_to_read texts still describe three-seed stored sets; and the script's review guard would treat any later edit of the record as covering the numbers.
